subject: Tile corners drawn with ggplot2 not rendered correctly

messages.author: 6d1cd0a71e6148df
messages.subject: Tile corners drawn with ggplot2 not rendered correctly
parts:
Hi!

I have found what I think *may* be considered a bug(let), but I'm not
sure it’s a bug in ggplot2 or in some other package. Example code:

library(ggplot2)
x=sample(1:10,3)
y=sample(1:10,3)
d=data.frame(x, y)
qplot(x,y,data=d, geom="tile", colour="foo", size=I(3))

On Windows the top-left corners of the rectangles have a small notch. It
basically looks like if each rectangle was drawn as a four-piece line
instead of a properly closed rectangle.

The curious thing is that if I run the same code on Linux, it looks OK.
And if I export the image as a PDF (on Windows), it looks OK. This leads
me to think that it’s just a problem with the default screen device on
Windows. And if I instead use CairoWin() from the Cairo package, it does
indeed look OK.

However, if I try do draw a rectangle just using grid commands, all the
corners look OK, *even on Windows*:

library(grid)
dev.off()
pushViewport(viewport())
grid.rect(gp=gpar(lwd=10, width=.1),x=.5, y=.5, width = unit(.5, "npc"),
height = unit(.5, "npc"))
dev.off()

So this leads me to suspect the way ggplot2 draws the rectangle isn’t
the ‘correct’/best way of doing it. Or am I wrong?


Regards,
Karl Ove Hufthammer

messages.subject: Re: Tile corners drawn with ggplot2 not rendered correctly
parts:
fr. den 09. 03. 2012 klokka 12.01 (+0100) skreiv Karl Ove Hufthammer:
> library(ggplot2)
> x=sample(1:10,3)
> y=sample(1:10,3)
> d=data.frame(x, y)
> qplot(x,y,data=d, geom="tile", colour="foo", size=I(3))
>
> On Windows the top-left corners of the rectangles have a small notch.
> It basically looks like if each rectangle was drawn as a four-piece
> line instead of a properly closed rectangle.

I believe the reason is that ‘geom-rect.R’ specifies ‘lineend="butt"’.
Changing this to ‘lineend="square", linejoin="mitre"’ should fix this.
I’m sure there is a reason that ‘geom-rect.R’ uses ‘lineend="butt"’,
but at least for ‘geom_tile’ square+mitre seems like a more sensible
value.

--
Karl Ove Hufthammer
